question: Which group was significantly affected by the British policy of resuming service tenures in Khurda?
solution:
**The correct answer is - Paiks**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Paiks**

 
 
• The Paiks were the traditional militia and landholders in Khurda.
 
• They were significantly affected by the British policy of resuming service tenures.
 
• This British policy essentially eliminated their service land grants, which were a crucial part of their livelihood.
 
• The resumption of these lands led to their financial and social destabilization.
 
• As a result, they were one of the primary groups to revolt during the Khurda Uprising.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamindars**

 
 
• Zamindars were the large landowners in Indian society who had certain privileges.
 
• They collected revenue from the ryots on behalf of the British government.
 
• Zamindars often wielded significant power and influence in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Ryots**
 
 
• Ryots were the peasants or tenant farmers who cultivated the land.
 
• They worked on the land and paid rent to the zamindars or directly to the British government.
 
• Ryots often faced exploitation and high revenue demands under colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Marathas**
 
 
• Marathas were a powerful warrior group from Maharashtra.
 
• They established a significant empire in central and western India during the 17th and 18th centuries.
 
• The Maratha Confederacy engaged in several wars against the British before their eventual defeat.
